# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤲 👈 👐]

The bomb shows display `0`, a green indicator, and five wires in order: red, yellow, green, white, blue. I need pass these visual facts to the Mute, who can consult the manual and then tell the Blind exactly what to do. I will also ask the Mute to relay the manual’s procedure aloud to the Blind, since speech is the only route to the hands.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0. Indicator light is green. Wires from position 1 to 5 are red, yellow, green, white, blue. Please read the manual for this configuration and speak the exact required action to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤝]

The visual configuration is unchanged. I have no established meaning for the gestures, so I cannot safely interpret them as bomb instructions. The Mute must use the manual and relay its exact procedure by speech to the Blind; I will restate the complete observed state and request that directly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="No gesture code was established, so I cannot interpret the gestures safely. The state remains display 0, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Use the manual and speak the exact operation and any required wire or button details to Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✌ 👇]

The bomb remains at display `0` with a green light and wires red, yellow, green, white, blue in positions 1–5. I still cannot know what the Mute has learned from the manual because I cannot hear speech, and the gestures have no agreed code. The Mute must give the Blind the exact manual-based instruction aloud; I should not guess from the gestures.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot interpret your gestures without an agreed code. Please immediately speak the exact manual instruction to Blind, including the required wire position or control and any timing.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 ✌ 🤝]

The bomb state is still unchanged. The Mute’s gestures are not a usable code because none was agreed beforehand, so I must not infer an instruction from them. The safest useful communication is to make clear to both teammates that the Mute must read the manual and verbally direct the Blind, who is the only one able to act.

``` 
speak(text="The state is unchanged: display 0, green light, wires red yellow green white blue. Mute, read the manual and tell Blind aloud the exact safe action. Blind, follow only the Mute's spoken manual instruction; do not act on these gestures.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. The Mute’s lone `✌` has no established meaning, so I cannot safely treat it as an instruction. I will establish a concrete gesture code now: the first gesture will identify the operation, and the second will identify a wire. Both Mute and Blind will hear the code; on the next turn I can interpret the Mute’s gestures and say the resulting instruction to Blind.

``` 
speak(text="Establishing code: Mute, send exactly two gestures after reading the manual. First gesture: 🤛 means cut, 🤜 means hold or press, ✊ means otherwise. Second gesture: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 wire 2, 👌 wire 3, ☝ wire 4, ✌ wire 5. Blind, I will announce the decoded instruction aloud. Current wires remain red, yellow, green, white, blue; display 0; light green.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤛 👎]

The Mute has sent the two gestures matching the code I established: `🤛` means cut, and `👎` means wire 2. Therefore the manual-directed action is to cut wire 2, the yellow wire. I will send that exact instruction to the Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Decoded manual instruction: cut wire 2, the yellow wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first action was accepted: the correct wire was cut. The bomb has changed and now shows a blue light; the remaining wires are green, white, blue, red in positions 1, 3, 4, 5, with position 2 cut. I will give the Mute the complete new visual state so the manual can determine the next action, and ask them to direct the Blind aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Correct wire was cut. New state: display 0, light blue. Wire 1 is green; wire 2 is CUT; wire 3 is white; wire 4 is blue; wire 5 is red. Read the manual for this updated state and tell Blind the exact next action aloud.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤛 👍]

The bomb is unchanged after the first successful cut: display `0`, blue light, and wire 1 green, wire 2 cut, wire 3 white, wire 4 blue, wire 5 red. Using our established code, `🤛` means cut and `👍` means wire 1. I will relay that instruction to the Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Decoded instruction: cut wire 1, the green wire.")
```
